50d712a2b01f5bc0: Keep this simple and auditable. Practical points, in general terms:
1e5debed9172926a: Pay against milestones, not requests. Stage payments should follow a schedule in the contract and a valuation of work done from the consultant. Treat any request for money "to secure materials" or "to keep the crew on site" outside that schedule as a conversation, not a payment.

4e33ce8178a57e0d: Keep a payment register. Every payment, its reference to a milestone or approved variation, and the supporting valuation. Reconcile it against the cost report monthly.
25adb6761a072176: Know what you are holding back. Retention and advance payment arrangements should be clear in the contract and tracked, because they are your main leverage at the end of the job.

6c8a87c2ce0f770b: How does UAE construction practice differ from the UK?
1ff799e24ce215fb: Owners who have built in the UK often assume the same rules apply. The principles are familiar, but several things are different.
ee8ba5098602c112: In the UK, most private residential work uses JCT forms, with an architect or contract administrator issuing instructions and certificates under the contract. In Dubai, the Municipality publishes standard forms for engineering consultancy and construction contracting for private villas (Dubai Municipality), and many projects use FIDIC-style terms. Read our guide to villa construction contracts in the UAE for more, and have any contract reviewed by a UAE-qualified lawyer.
6ae5e1fd623cd2d7: In Dubai, the registered consultant typically designs the villa, makes the authority submissions and carries the formal site role through construction, including assessing the contractor's payment applications. That is a regulated role. The owner appoints the consultant and the contractor separately, and the consultant's position sits between the two. An owner's representative such as Eastbridge is a different role: we act only for the owner, alongside the consultant and the contractor, and do not replace either. Our article on owner's representative vs project manager vs consultant explains the difference.
51864663f6de00d8: UAE law imposes a ten-year liability on the main contractor and the engineer for serious structural defects, now set out in Articles 821 to 824 of the new Civil Code in force from 1 June 2026; it cannot be contracted out of (Charles Russell Speechlys). There is no direct UK equivalent for a one-off private house, though the protection is narrower than many owners assume. Take legal advice on how it applies to you.
9c071125f4af66c4: UK residential contractors are used to clients who visit regularly and argue every variation. In Dubai, the volume of work and the spread of contractor capability are both wide. Some firms run well-documented, transparent jobs. Others rely on the owner not being there. Your reporting regime tells the contractor which kind of client you are.
b4d922aef7817dae: Common failure modes for absentee owners
97496a27e16b4129: Every builder sees these from the other side of the table. They are not unique to Dubai, but distance makes each one worse.
d4fc04337725d5c6: Verbal approvals. A quick "yes, fine" on a call becomes a variation nobody priced. Every approval should go into the decision log, in writing, with its cost.
bde9b4983535a018: Payments ahead of progress. Once the contractor has been paid for work not yet done, your leverage has gone. This is the single most common way absentee builds get into trouble.
70e2ee5df93d2e32: Design that was never truly frozen. Small changes during construction cost far more than the same changes on paper, and each one gives the contractor a legitimate reason to ask for more time.
0787fa3d0dbc075c: Provisional sums left vague. On the contractor's side, the first thing we looked at on any job was where the provisional sums sat and how loosely they were described. That is where final accounts grow.
8a0161c03308a21f: Nobody independent looking. Photographs chosen by the contractor show what the contractor wants you to see. An independent visit, unannounced where possible, sees what is actually there.
baf4803a6e27db0d: Late finishes decisions. If you have not chosen tiles, sanitaryware or joinery when the programme needs them, the delay is yours, and so is the cost.
abe0baa9839cf2d6: Handover from a distance. Accepting the keys without a proper snagging inspection usually means a long defects period of chasing by email.

cda73b008065a95b: The process is well defined. Dubai Municipality's "Building in Dubai" platform, launched in October 2023, covers the whole life of a project: land, design, permits, construction, completion, connection and later alterations. Since 2022, building permits across Dubai Municipality, the Dubai Development Authority, Trakhees and DIEZ go through a single unified e-window, with Civil Defence, RTA, DEWA, Etisalat and du linked in.
79476074106394e6: Durations without a label are from Real Estate Club Dubai. The others are our own planning allowances and depend heavily on the owner's speed of decision.
4f73135fd39f3f0e: Stage 1: Check the plot before you commit
e4aac1c5fc4276ea: Before you buy, or before you design on a plot you already own, establish what can be built on it. That means the plot affection plan, the master developer's design guidelines, setbacks, height and coverage limits, existing utility connections, access, and any outstanding service charges or developer conditions. Ground conditions and the water table matter too; a basement on a waterfront plot is a very different exercise from one inland.
df3014e9ed175cd6: Who does what: the owner commissions the checks; the consultant interprets planning and design constraints; a UAE-qualified lawyer should review title and any developer agreements. Our guide to plot checks in Dubai goes through them in detail.
e848505fc5727e2e: Stage 2: Set the brief and the budget
9b39691aba5816c3: The brief is the most valuable document in the project and the cheapest to change. Bedrooms, basement or not, pool, staff quarters, home automation, the level of finish, how you will live in the house. Write it down and attach a budget built from the full cost picture, not just a rate per square foot. Our article on what it costs to build a villa in Dubai sets out every line.
2ad87740a592c1cf: Stage 3: Appoint your consultant and design the villa
e086eb24add83974: Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, engineering consultancy in Dubai, including in free zones, may only be practised by registered firms (Al Tamimi). Your consultant designs the villa across architecture, structure and MEP, prepares the drawings for approval, and normally carries the statutory site role during construction. Dubai Municipality publishes standard contract forms for consultancy and construction on private villas, in Arabic, which are a useful baseline.
0d67345cd19f5db5: The BPS app, relaunched in August 2024, includes a registry and ratings for consultants and contractors, and is worth checking before you appoint. Design normally runs from concept through to detailed design. Every hour spent resolving detail at this stage is cheaper than any hour spent resolving it on site.
acd3e8accf44aaa3: Stage 4: Master-developer NOC and building permit
22cb4a4e0f7fdd70: In a master-planned community, the master developer reviews the design against its guidelines and issues its NOC. In Nakheel communities, for example, renovation and extension approvals begin with a Nakheel NOC application through its portal before the authority permit.
f217e39bb6c8214a: The authority permit then runs through Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Under Dubai Municipality's residential procedure, the consultant or contractor submits drawings and fees online, the service-authority NOCs are issued through the unified window, and the permit is issued with stamped drawings. In August 2026, Dubai Municipality announced an AI system that checks villa drawings against the Dubai Building Code, being rolled out in phases through Build in Dubai (Khaleej Times). In practice, cleaner drawings should mean fewer rounds of comments.
3b3e29052ab00dc2: Who does what: the consultant prepares and submits; the master developer and authority review and approve; the owner pays fees and answers design questions quickly.
6b6b28c8699cdf4c: Run a competitive process on a complete design. Your consultant normally prepares the bid package; you, as owner, decide who is invited and who is appointed. Compare bids like-for-like: scope, exclusions, provisional sums, preliminaries, programme, payment terms and retention. The lowest number is not automatically the lowest cost. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai explains what to look for, and our guide to villa construction contracts covers the agreement itself. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer before signing.
78f49084b1837dbd: The contractor mobilises, builds and manages the site. The authority inspects at defined stages; Dubai Municipality's procedure refers to staged inspections such as shoring, foundations and slabs. Your consultant fulfils the statutory site role. Monthly valuations measure work done, and you pay against them.
4e6610437dbd8acb: The owner's job during construction is to make decisions on time, approve samples and mock-ups, and keep an independent view of cost and programme. On the contractor's side, we always knew which clients read the monthly report and which did not. The ones who did not were the ones whose sites drifted.
ea5460d38cdac5ba: At the end, Dubai Municipality's procedure describes a joint completion inspection involving Building Control, Survey, telecoms and Civil Defence where needed, followed by the completion certificate and service connection. In parallel, the villa is snagged, defects are listed and rectified, operating manuals and warranties are handed over, and the defects liability period begins. Our villa snagging checklist covers what to inspect.

1436febc0ed78d02: Which decisions cost the most if made late?
2198a914ec5c7f7f: In our experience, these are the decisions that are cheap at design stage and expensive afterwards:
056627216884b190: Basement or no basement. It changes structure, waterproofing, shoring, excavation and programme. Adding one late is effectively a redesign.
714fe8e8945f7253: Overall size and layout. Moving walls after the permit can mean resubmission and lost months.
cd91992e8055b6cd: Glazing and openings. Large-format and structural glazing has long lead times and drives the structure around it.
f13351fba7036b21: MEP strategy. Cooling, home automation, AV and lighting control need their routes and plant space designed in. Adding them later means chasing walls and ceilings.
b744f42c7d7b1af8: Pool and external works. These interact with structure, drainage and levels.
c8dfd0d924572b9d: Finishes and specification. Stone, joinery and sanitaryware chosen late are usually priced as variations, without competition.
126434aa33d3c496: From the builder's side, a late change was rarely a problem for the contractor. It was an opportunity. That is not cynicism, just how the commercial model works.
f0eb62c90428fab3: How do you keep a villa build on programme?
e988fcc181cd18ed: Most delay on a private villa is not caused by bad weather or a shortage of labour. 01b52dde5d80f264: Agree a decision schedule at the start. List every choice the owner has to make, from tiles to door handles to automation scenes, with the latest date each can be made without holding up the work. Ask the contractor to confirm the dates against its programme.
aa1ea13e1c36490c: Answer site questions quickly. Every request for information from the contractor should have a named person responsible and a target response time. Unanswered questions turn into delay claims.
d4f6a06f5e7a3619: Review progress against the programme monthly, not just against payments. A valuation tells you what has been paid for. The programme tells you whether the villa will be finished when you expect. Both need reading together.
61d8ef2c9a461d62: If you are building from abroad, these habits matter even more, because decisions made by email across time zones take longer. Our guide to building a villa in Dubai from the UK covers how to set this up.

d3c49334c9422f30: 3. Who will run our site, and can we meet them?
29402c93caec02a6: The site manager or project manager who turns up every day decides the quality of your villa. Ask for names and CVs of the key staff, ask whether they will be dedicated to your project, and ask what happens if they leave. Make the named people a condition of the contract where you can.
11740e2418d3e170: On the contractor's side, we knew that the strongest site manager went to the job with the most demanding client and the best-run paperwork. That is not cynicism; it is how a builder protects its reputation with limited resources.
4af5926923d42f7c: 4. Is your price based on our drawings and specification, with nothing substituted?
3b1b27ad985913cf: Ask every bidder to confirm in writing that they have priced the documents as issued, and to list any alternatives separately. Substituted products and "equivalent" finishes buried in the pricing are a common way of shaving a headline number.
08bfcbf82f4d1a8b: Preliminaries are the cost of running the site rather than building the villa: site staff, welfare, hoarding, temporary power and water, insurance, scaffolding, plant, cleaning and waste. Turner & Townsend put contractor preliminaries in Dubai at 12–14% in 2025 (cited by PRASOON). A bid with preliminaries far below that range is either very efficient or has moved costs elsewhere, or has left them out to be claimed later. Ask for a breakdown, and ask how the monthly figure changes if the programme extends.
82efea7e8c3061f1: 6. What provisional sums have you included, and why?
d75f797a523296e3: A provisional sum is an allowance for work that cannot yet be fully defined. They are legitimate in small numbers. Large or numerous provisional sums mean the true price is still unknown. When comparing bids, list every provisional sum side by side and, where possible, set common figures for all bidders so the comparison is fair.
1c1273ef870bc755: Read exclusions as carefully as the price. Pools, landscaping, external works, kitchens, wardrobes, lighting control, AV, authority fees and service connections are frequently excluded or qualified. Two bids with the same total can be several hundred thousand dirhams apart once exclusions are priced back in.
7b7f2d6d3d9df39b: 8. What is your programme, and what does it depend on?
cf9463ea721df7de: Ask for a programme showing the main stages, the critical path and what the contractor needs from you and when: design information, selections, approvals, payments. A programme that looks fast but depends on you making every decision instantly is not a real programme. See how long it takes to build a villa in Dubai for typical durations.
9ca22c869368ab18: 9. Can we speak to your last three villa clients?
3c82c46e8ed3c158: Not the three the contractor chooses to show off; the last three completed. And call them. Useful questions are: did the final account match the contract price, and if not, why? Was completion on time? How were defects handled after handover? Would you use them again? Whenever you can, visit a finished villa and a live site.
5b158022384c0a93: 10. What payment terms are you asking for?
abd1edb593068d84: Avoid schedules that pay large sums upfront or against calendar dates. Payments should follow work actually completed and checked. Agree how each payment is valued, who checks it and how long you have to pay once it is agreed. Our article on villa construction contracts in the UAE covers how payments are valued in more detail.
7747a6af8bf758f0: 11. What security will you provide: bonds, retention, insurance?
f53a5982231d048c: Ask whether the contractor will provide an advance payment guarantee against any mobilisation payment, a performance bond, and accept retention held back until completion and the end of the defects period. Ask for evidence of contractors' all-risks and third-party insurance. A contractor that resists all of these is telling you something about its balance sheet.
e74659f4f75f3f50: 12. How do you handle changes and delays?
728769a0db524e55: Every villa changes during construction. Ask how the contractor prices variations, how quickly it gives you a cost before carrying out changed work, and how it notifies delays. A clear answer here predicts a calmer project. A vague answer predicts arguments.
cf6d0fa639a8df60: Once the bids are in, put them on one page before anyone looks at the bottom line.
d5b393b6e39652b0: Then hold a short clarification meeting with each serious bidder. Ask the same questions of each, record the answers, and have any changes confirmed in writing before you decide.
0acfd154143c990e: Red flags when choosing a contractor
27984e0bd976ef17: A price far below the others, with no clear explanation.
c8fb38343b1f63db: Pressure to sign quickly, or to pay a deposit before the contract is agreed.
4e6dda5bca162369: Reluctance to name the site team or provide references.
c718f37d978e85b4: Heavy qualifications, long exclusions or "subject to" language throughout the bid.
e1d99e9b548eaa69: Payment schedules weighted to the front of the job.
b4c135e84a916b17: No appetite for bonds, retention or proper insurance.
66320d07271cb963: Suggestions that work can start before the permit is in place.
167ecd229cbfbbf9: A firm that cannot show you a finished villa of comparable quality.
3a00ae91ac7b0719: What a good contractor wants to see from you
c09043b4c6e2f57b: This is the part owners rarely hear. From our years on the builder's side, the best contractors choose their clients as carefully as clients choose them, and they price accordingly.
88a2f5cd34900a72: A good contractor wants to see:
713d9c0cd0f70d15: Complete drawings and a clear specification. Uncertainty is priced as risk. The clearer the documents, the sharper the price.
32e40de6287a7710: A decisive client. Late selections and changing minds are what delay villas. A contractor who sees an organised decision process prices less contingency.
a9997156d061edf9: Proof the money is there. Contractors worry about being paid. Clear payment terms, a sensible cash flow and a track record of paying on time make you a preferred client.
5b3168a32dc1a8e1: A fair contract. One-sided terms do not make a project safer; they make good contractors walk away and leave the bidders who plan to recover their margin through claims.
f3bbda2089d82587: Someone on the client side who understands construction. Contractors prefer dealing with a knowledgeable client representative to dealing with confusion. Disputes are expensive for them too.
656d723c00ba9f97: On the contractor's side, the jobs we priced keenest were the ones where the drawings were finished, the client knew what they wanted, and we trusted we would be paid on time. Those are all things an owner controls.

c79e779533e1bde8: How many contractors should I ask to bid?
87154dd956eb512a: In our experience three to five serious bidders is enough. Fewer gives you no comparison; more wastes everyone's time and the best firms may decline to price a long list.
6ab050e1c36ecc6c: Should I just take the lowest price?
59de6d4afd5fdb3c: Not without normalising the bids first. The lowest headline figure often has the thinnest preliminaries, the largest provisional sums or the longest list of exclusions, and the difference comes back as variations.

63f13016d484f5b2: A project manager organises the project; an owner's representative does that and acts solely for the owner, with no stake in the design or the build.

10188c1aa286d07d: What should you ask before appointing an owner's representative?
7f83f3fa467e617d: On a Dubai villa build, your registered consultant designs the house and carries the statutory technical role, your contractor builds it, and an owner's representative acts solely for you on cost, programme, contract and decisions. A "project manager" can be any of these things depending on who employs them, which is why the title matters less than whose interests the person serves. The roles complement each other; none replaces the consultant.
1a4913b743a9e049: What does each role actually do?
24ac0283ae82eee8: The confusion is understandable. In the UAE, "project manager", "owner's rep", "PMC" and "consultant" are used loosely, and firms describe themselves differently. Focus on function and on who pays them.
0e867e1f9d9cd404: Owner, within professional and statutory duties
3e6864f744a00e56: No; reviews design against brief and budget
6a407bc52dcbc048: Helps the owner compare like-for-like and choose
28a0339ec62c22f5: The consultant role is defined by law. Under Dubai Law No. 14 of 2025, only registered consultancies may practise engineering consultancy or present themselves as engineering consultants, and the law applies across Dubai including free zones (Al Tamimi). The other two roles are defined by contract.
ae76874b1df5f6ff: Your consultant is your designer and your statutory technical professional. They take the brief, design the villa, coordinate the engineering, prepare and submit the approval drawings, and normally carry the statutory site role during construction. They are essential. You cannot build without one. Dubai Municipality publishes standard consultancy contract forms for private villas, in Arabic, and the BPS app lists registered consultants with ratings.
4ae195227a1d9a4a: "Project manager" describes an activity, not an allegiance. A contractor has project managers. Some consultants offer project management as an add-on. Some independent firms offer it to owners. The work is planning, coordinating, chasing and reporting. Before you rely on a project manager, ask who appoints them and who pays them.
f7d9bb543ccb8306: An owner's representative manages the project from the owner's side of the table only. Typical scope: setting and controlling the budget, the programme and the decision schedule; helping the owner compare bids and choose; reviewing valuations and variations; independent client-side site visits and reporting; and keeping the consultant and contractor accountable to the brief. The owner's representative does not design, does not make authority submissions and does not take on the consultant's statutory role. The value lies in having no stake in the design fee or the construction price.
97d78aa2f79c2f57: Owers House, Feock, Cornwall. Built by P Chapman Construction.
c8d73c20a5a75653: Where are the conflicts of interest?
999b106841209b05: Every party on a villa build has a legitimate commercial interest. Conflicts arise when one party is asked to check its own work.
f3ff61bd1b788d22: Design-and-build firms. One company designs, prices and builds. That can be efficient, with a single point of responsibility. But the same firm decides how much building the design contains, prices it, and then prices every change. Nobody independent is testing whether the design is efficient or the price is fair, unless you arrange it.
995720c1c45ef05c: Consultants checking their own design. When the consultant who designed the villa also reviews the contractor's claims for design-related changes, they are judging, in part, their own drawings. Most consultants handle this professionally. But a variation caused by a design gap is a difficult thing for the designer to call. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned villa consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating build costs, suspending two offices for six months (Gulf News). A design that is heavier than it needs to be is expensive, and the person best placed to spot it is not the person who drew it.
06bdf7809dce3594: Fees tied to construction value. Consultant fees in Dubai are commonly a percentage of construction cost. That is market practice, not wrongdoing, but it means nobody on a percentage fee is rewarded for making the building cheaper.
9d7a69a4207f2f2f: Contractor-employed project managers. The contractor's project manager is there to deliver the contractor's job profitably. That is their job. It is not the same job as protecting your budget.
fffb61199f1fd3b1: Anyone who has run a building company knows the pattern: projects where the client has no independent adviser are commercially easier for the contractor. Provisional sums go unquestioned, variation rates go untested and monthly valuations are rarely challenged. Nobody is doing anything wrong. There is simply no one asking.
4eee4187fb2c559f: Whatever you call the role, put it in writing. Take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on the final form.

03cac42ba396a845: When do you need an owner's representative, and when don't you?
e9b1306704d55409: To be straightforward about it, not every villa needs one.
b1fc51fc1b38528c: You probably do not need one if the villa is relatively simple, the design is complete before pricing, you have built before, you live in Dubai, you have time to attend site and read the monthly reports, and you trust your consultant to act firmly on your behalf with the contractor. 4fc46f36a9a95659: What should you ask before appointing an owner's representative?
2e66d2b78dc94277: If you decide you want one, test the fit before you sign. These are the questions we would ask in your position:
fb3dca9e81f677df: Who else pays you on this project? The only acceptable answer is nobody. Ask whether they receive referral fees, commissions or any other benefit from consultants, contractors or suppliers.
530954d442a9eb54: What have you built, and from which side? Experience on the contractor's side, the consultant's side or the developer's side gives different strengths. Ask for specifics, and be wary of anyone who claims experience they cannot describe in detail.
c6959a4cff9066bb: What exactly will you deliver each month? A sample report tells you more than a brochure.
e0cd224180fb3072: How often will you be on site, and who will come? Agree the frequency and the person, not just the firm.
1ded210355b1f85b: What will you not do? A good owner's representative is clear about the boundary with your registered consultant, and will not claim to design, make authority submissions or take on the consultant's statutory role.
91d9ca49b363df59: How is the fee structured? A fixed or time-based fee against a defined scope keeps incentives cleaner than a percentage of construction value.
0131cad73515fa12: An honest answer to the last question often tells you more than the others.

f1c8335334a2b110: Who approves a villa renovation on Palm Jumeirah?
db5e29679f1a8c7d: Palm Jumeirah is a Nakheel master community. That means two layers of approval sit above your design.
f1fc589b8171b56f: The master developer. Renovation and extension approvals in Nakheel communities start with an NOC application through Nakheel's portal. Nakheel is checking that your proposal respects the community's design guidelines, plot limits and frontage rules, and that the works will be carried out in a way that does not disrupt neighbours or damage shared infrastructure. Expect to submit drawings, contractor details and, for larger work, a deposit or undertaking.
a85e8997b1564590: The permitting authority. With the NOC in hand, your registered consultant applies for the building permit from Dubai Municipality, Trakhees or the Dubai Development Authority, depending on where your plot sits. Since 2022 Dubai has run a single unified e-window for building permits across these authorities, with Civil Defence, RTA, DEWA and the telecoms providers linked in, so the NOCs from service authorities are gathered through one system rather than door to door. The Build in Dubai platform now covers alterations as well as new builds.
7b8986fd4f037371: The owner appoints the consultant and the contractor. The consultant prepares and submits the drawings; the contractor carries out the work under the permit. Our role at Eastbridge is to represent you alongside both, not to replace either.

6c0c9b6955954a1d: What hidden problems do older Palm villas have?
80f5e14c4ecfe31b: Many of the original frond villas are now around two decades old. They were built quickly, at scale, in a demanding marine environment. In our experience the same issues come up again and again on coastal houses of that age, wherever they are.
40bfd2d449bb25d5: Roof membranes, wet-room tanking, terraces over habitable rooms and basement waterproofing all have a finite life. Failures often show as staining, blistering paint or musty rooms long after the damage has started. Replacing a roof or basement membrane is not a cosmetic job; it means stripping finishes, possibly lifting screeds, and doing it before any new interior goes in.
8c8c664a32558cf2: Air-conditioning systems, ductwork, pipework and electrical distribution installed when the villa was built may be near the end of their life or undersized for how you want to live now. If you are replacing finishes, it is almost always cheaper to replace tired services at the same time than to open the villa up again in three years.

50e83327c9d47830: Payments should follow work done, not the calendar. A sound process looks like this:

8d67b6ed9b33ca54: A variation is any change to the work described in the contract: an added room, a different finish, a moved wall, an omission. Variations are normal. Unmanaged variations are the single biggest cause of budget overruns we have seen.

efe374166640755d: Instruction in writing. Only the person named in the contract can instruct a change, and only in writing.
1245925677cf86c1: Quotation before work. The contractor prices the change, including any effect on time, before carrying it out.
de975e63d6c5f62a: Agreement. The owner accepts, rejects or negotiates the cost and time.
d1483afa7ae4a702: Record. The agreed variation is logged and carried into the next payment and the running final account.

20a37e0a13ddd57a: How snag lists get closed out, and how they stall
e2cef83c5a60f80c: We spent two decades on the contractor's side of handovers. Here is what we know about how they go.
fe87a0079a3caa26: A clean, numbered list. A contractor's site manager can allocate a numbered list to trades in an hour. A vague list becomes an argument.
6da456bfbdd16e23: One list, one owner. When the owner, the family, the interior designer and the consultant all send separate lists, items get duplicated, contradicted and lost.
bc4ac1278945ac17: Money still on the table. On the contractor's side, the jobs we closed out fastest were the ones where a meaningful sum was still to be paid on completion.
9417eec2be92a028: Joint walkrounds. Walking the list together, item by item, and signing off what is closed stops the same items being reopened.
face78755c488ad1: Early release of money. Once the final payment and retention have gone, the snag list competes with every other job for the contractor's attention. It usually loses.
1ff2def5aa55e839: Trades demobilised. Subcontractors leave site once their package is paid. Getting a tiler back for three tiles is hard for the main contractor too.
226b6a7c659e08b1: Snags mixed with changes. If the list includes things you have changed your mind about, the contractor will treat the whole list as a variation request. Separate defects from new requests.
f19fc567df69af53: Moving in too early. Once furniture and family are in, it becomes difficult to prove who caused a scratch or a chip. Inspect and record before occupation.
27740973c294f1bf: No deadline. Agree a date for closing items, in writing, as part of handover.

75d125cae4d73f67: A builder knows that the price you sign is a starting point, that the margin on a job is often planned in the gaps rather than the headline, and that most owners never read the documents where those gaps sit. Provisional sums, preliminaries, variation rates, programme float and the monthly valuation are where a villa's real cost is decided. We spent 21 years on the contractor's side of premium residential building in the UK, and this is what we would want any owner to know before signing.
ea20ace8a35b4d6f: Nothing here is a criticism of contractors. Building is a hard, risky business with thin margins, and a good contractor is worth paying properly. But the commercial logic of the contractor's side is not the owner's logic, and the owner who understands it gets a better building for less trouble.
1accb36cbead3cb9: How does a contractor actually price a villa bid?
b604cbc7b4b3f359: Owners imagine a contractor adds up materials and labour, puts a margin on top, and sends the number. That is the estimate. The bid is something else.
b09a76d7373cd7f0: On the contractor's side, the first thing any builder prices is not the building. It is the risk in the documents. How complete was the design? Which items were vague? What was missing from the drawings that would obviously have to be built? Where would the client inevitably change their mind? Those answers decide how a contractor bids.
371decc595d9eb32: When the design is complete and the competition strong, contractors price tight, because there is little to recover later. When the design is loose, the market can afford to bid lower, because everyone knows the job will grow. That is the uncomfortable truth: an incomplete design does not just add risk, it invites a lower bid, which looks like good news to the owner and is often the opposite.
a02e137d787cf174: Contractors also price the client. A first-time owner who lives overseas, with no independent adviser, is a different commercial proposition from an experienced developer with a quantity surveyor checking every valuation. Nobody writes that on the bid, but it is in the number.
e834f43a7300ce53: Then there is the subcontract market. Much of a villa is built by specialist subcontractors: MEP, glazing, joinery, stone, pools. The main contractor's bid depends on quotes from them, and those quotes can be sharpened after the main contract is signed. Savings found after signature are the contractor's to keep unless the contract says otherwise.

cfc12f4d15906d27: What are provisional sums, and why do they matter so much?
c1cfc04cd3034bf3: A provisional sum is an allowance for something not yet designed or chosen. "Kitchen: AED X." "Lighting control: AED Y." When the actual item is selected, the contract sum moves to the real cost.
9d0299fb06eb7b5a: From the builder's side, provisional sums do three useful things for the contractor:
56f6c0b4b0204f50: They make the bid look lower. If the owner's documents leave the allowance to the contractor, a low allowance makes the total more competitive, and the real cost arrives later.
a620eedcd76ec7de: They move risk to the owner. Whatever the item eventually costs, the owner pays it.
aad16285582c7e15: They often carry their own mark-up and attendance. Read how the contract adjusts provisional sums: is the contractor's overhead and profit added to the difference, and is there extra time?
6a5c6cbf0cbd6c98: In Dubai, this is particularly relevant on luxury villas, where kitchens, wardrobes, lighting, automation, AV and loose specialist items are often left as allowances because the owner has not chosen yet. In our experience, a bid where these make up a large share of the total is not really a fixed price at all.
c0cc2c2733cf23fd: What to do: resolve as many items as you can before pricing. Where you cannot, set the provisional sums yourself, at realistic levels, so every bidder carries the same figure. Then compare bids on what is left.
e1193dc8e56e25a4: Why are preliminaries the line to watch?
0c50770a21dbfb09: Preliminaries are the cost of running the site: the site manager, welfare, security, temporary power and water, scaffolding, hoarding, plant, insurances, waste and so on. Turner & Townsend put contractor preliminaries in Dubai at 12–14% (as cited by PRASOON).
6b1fcaff67d0e8b1: The important point is that many preliminaries are time-related. They are priced per week or per month. That means:
4c022a6f1173b0a0: A contractor who prices a short programme can show a low preliminaries figure. If the programme then slips, the time-related costs reappear in an extension-of-time claim.
955d5a8249272ef9: Every week of delay that the contract attributes to the owner, through late decisions, late information or changes, carries a weekly cost.
3138e47bf0bbce3a: When we compared our own bids against competitors, an unusually low preliminaries figure usually meant one of two things: an unrealistic programme, or preliminary costs hidden elsewhere in the rates. Ask every bidder for a weekly breakdown of time-related preliminaries. It tells you what delay will cost before it happens.
adf3cd245d5b4c94: A variation is a change to the work. Some are genuine owner changes. Many are not; they arise because the drawings were unclear, two consultants' drawings disagreed, or something necessary was simply missing.
37c6e900787db739: On the contractor's side, the commercial team reads the contract documents looking for exactly these gaps, from the day the job is won. Every ambiguity is a potential variation. Every late answer to a request for information is a potential delay. This is ordinary practice, and a contractor who did not do it would not stay in business for long.
80e5cd6ecb57f28e: How a variation claim is typically assembled:
a8e2287beba62c10: The direct cost of the extra or changed work, priced at contract rates where they apply and at new rates where they do not. New rates are where the margin tends to be.
ff343252218ebe5a: Knock-on costs: work removed or redone, materials wasted, re-sequencing.
84301f53e336863e: Time: if the change affects the critical path, an extension of time, and with it time-related preliminaries.
27f577c61568ba7d: Disruption: loss of productivity from working out of sequence.
dc5fa31de6d57d3c: The defence is the same in every case: price the variation and agree its time effect before it is instructed, in writing. A variation agreed after the work is done is priced by one party, the one that did it. We cover the contractual side in villa construction contracts in the UAE; take advice from a UAE-qualified lawyer on your specific contract.
5ec4074138842ccf: Float is the slack in a programme: the amount an activity can slip without delaying completion. Owners rarely think about it. Contractors think about it a great deal.
8c41b51aae280f74: If the contract is silent, the practical answer is usually that float is used by whoever needs it first. A contractor who has planned well keeps float in its own activities and presents a programme where the owner's decisions sit on the critical path, with no slack. Then any late owner decision, a tile not chosen, a sample not approved, causes immediate, claimable delay.
116c1d3fea041ec3: When reviewing a contractor's programme, look for:
9521fa44ffb67880: Owner decisions shown with no float, while the contractor's own activities have plenty.
086c7eadd94f5eb9: Durations for long-lead items that assume orders the owner has not yet been asked to approve.
ed424bfff8fa72d4: A programme without a clear list of information required from the owner, and when.
ac2d7990d4acb771: A decision schedule, agreed at the start, listing every owner choice and the latest date it can be made without delay, is one of the cheapest protections an owner can have.
470ff7ca4ae9436e: Why is the cheapest bid rarely the cheapest outcome?
790e78d56befab5c: Put the pieces together. The lowest bid often has some combination of low provisional sums, tight exclusions, a short programme with low preliminaries, and keen rates on the measured work but generous scope to recover through new rates. It may also have been priced by a contractor who needs the turnover.
5cbcf23dd2ec455a: None of that is visible in the total. It is visible in the breakdown, which is why bids should be compared line by line, with provisional sums normalised, exclusions priced back in, and preliminaries tested against a realistic programme. Our guide to choosing a villa contractor in Dubai shows how.
fb5ca5cc57a67aa7: There is one more factor: design. In August 2025, Dubai Municipality warned villa consultancies about over-designing structures and inflating build costs (Gulf News). A competitive bid on an over-designed villa is still a bid for more building than you need.
2455858710e80216: How should you read a monthly valuation?
e4c0226a49ba3603: Each month the contractor submits a valuation: the value of work done to date, less previous payments and retention. On the contractor's side, the valuation was also a cash-flow tool, and it was normal to value optimistically. Front-loading, valuing early activities generously so cash arrives ahead of cost, is common practice across the industry.
6a3e83b6ec6d1869: Read a valuation line by line:
f23e508a7497ab97: Is the work actually installed? Not delivered, not "in progress", installed. Materials on site are a separate question, and paying for materials off site needs proof of ownership and insurance.
429e2d911acdc262: Do percentages match what you see? If the electrical installation is valued at 60%, is 60% of it actually done?
c99e6fb345c89b3a: Are variations valued only once agreed? Unagreed variations should be shown separately, not slipped into the total.
ffdaa57b9fb24d87: Does the cumulative value track the programme? A valuation running ahead of physical progress is a warning sign, especially if the contractor's position is weakening.

7266580bec24c4fd: Practical completion and handover is the moment the balance of power shifts. Before it, the contractor wants the final payments, the release of part of the retention, and to stop paying for the site. After it, they have moved their team to the next job.
f2c53d773fbdd645: From the builder's side, we always knew which defects would be fixed promptly: the ones listed before handover, while money was still held. Defects raised months later, with retention already released, joined a queue.
5bd71b959d77e401: Snag thoroughly before accepting handover, with an independent inspection, not just a walk-round. Our villa snagging checklist is a starting point.
806701ec4b086382: Do not release payments or retention until agreed defects are rectified, within what your contract allows.
96ebd9e14f844c59: Insist on as-built drawings, operating manuals, warranties and test certificates before handover, not after.
d93ff7acdaf7f3ce: Know your defects liability period and diarise inspections well before it ends.
